missing_evidence: Payment service logs/metrics around 03:30-03:31 UTC to explain 503 on /v1/authorizations
candidates.statement: Checkout 502s originate downstream: gateway POST /v1/checkout returns 502 because order returns 502, and order's payment call fails with 503 Service Unavailable on /v1/authorizations. Inventory/redis reservations succeed (200), so the failure is the payment dependency, not gateway or inventory.
candidates.uncertainty: No payment-side logs or metrics admitted; payment 503 root cause (config, saturation, crash) unconfirmed.

report.explanation: Traces show a consistent chain: gateway /v1/checkout 502 <- order /v1/orders 502 <- payment /v1/authorizations 503, while inventory reservations return 200. Gateway metrics show 502s only on /v1/checkout with low latency (~94ms p95), consistent with fast downstream error propagation rather than gateway-local fault. Payment-side evidence is absent, so the bounded candidate is downstream payment failure causing checkout 502s.
